70.t: The Chu Berry automobile accident near Youngstown
70.s: On the road to Toronto the bus came on Lamar Wright's overturned car; Chu Berry was injured with a skull fracture and was delirious.
70.q: But, you know, one of the greatest things that I'll never forget with that band -- of course, there was so many great things happened even when I first come into the band the changes that went on in the band and everything. I'll never forget the night that poor Choo, that we was on the way from…

70.s: Hinton produces the pipe and watch he picked up at the crash scene and recalls Chu's delirious words about his change.
70.q: See, that's the pipe he had in the automobile accident, and he picked it up. There it is.

70.s: Brown, unused to the fluid-drive car, braked into a skid and hit a bridge; Chu Berry was thrown clear and, delirious, hit a doctor at the hospital.
70.q: Uh-huh. Well, you know how that happened? You see, you know, Brown was driving. Lamar let him drive. The car was a fluid drive.

70.t: Chu Berry's death and the minute of silence in Montreal
70.s: Chu died days later; Calloway waited until after the dance in Montreal to announce it and hired a replacement.
70.q: And he told the people, he said, 'Now we'll have a minute's silence for a brother of ours that passed this morning.' And we didn't know that Calloway had sent and got his mother --

418.t: Speed Webb's arrangers and the car that went into the canal
418.s: Speed Webb's band had seven arrangers, one of whom, Chuck Ross, died when his car went off the road into a canal in Canada.
418.q: It was a good band. All the bands I played with they were -- they were very good bands. Especially Steve Webb. I tell you Steve Webb had one of the greatest bands -- it's just too bad it never did get recorded. And it's too bad Thamon Hayes never did get recorded at the time, you know. But --

432.t: Killing on the bandstand; the Washingtons and Nat Tolles's band
432.s: They recap the death, and Lewis names Booker and Willie Washington and Nat Tolles's band.
432.ch: On the road with Victor Spencer
432.q: Yeah, that's right. Yeah. You see? Because I was in that section with those outfits. Did you play with them too? And they had Al, Booker's cousin Al, Al of Washington, Al, he died in Chicago, used to play tenor. Al was playing tenor with us out there.

84.t: Toots Johnson's band personnel and the fatal car accident
84.s: Handy names the leading bands outside New Orleans and Toots Johnson's sidemen, then tells of a crash that killed bassist Mal.
84.ch: Tom Albert and Baton Rouge bands
84.q: And he'd sing a lot of them. Did a lot of singing. But he didn't play anything. Oh, he had a playhouse in his yard, though. That thing was around 12 by 12 was a little girl. He had a real funny to play. He was a great guy. He was a great guy. for his little girl. They had real furniture in there…

17.t: Chu Berry's fatal auto accident and the bus fire
17.s: Cab's band came upon the wreck; Chu died, and the bus caught fire that night.
17.ch: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
17.q: CC: That's right, and what happened that night, well they were in the car with Lamar Wright, Vernon Brown and Chu, and of course all of us were at the bus and we had to wait until the band boy loaded the bus, so we were half hour behind. So Cab, that Christmas Cab would always buy the band a nice…

31.t: Copying for Russell Wooding at the Riviera
31.s: Whaley copied music for arranger Russell Wooding's show at the Riviera across the Hudson, and recalls how Wooding died in a fire.
31.ch: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
31.q: Yeah, we went there in the dead of winter like. We was all in our overcoats working and they had heaters going on and we were arranging the music. Russell Wooding.

124.t: Cab Calloway calls after Chu Berry's accident
124.s: Cab's manager found McRae on Broadway and sent him to Toronto and Montreal, where he learned Berry had died.
124.ch: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
124.q: And I was around New York the year that Chu Berry had that accident. And the day that he had the accident, Cab Calloway knew he needed a tenor player, and so he wired Mittler, his manager, 1619 Broadway, to come in --

473.t: The night Chu Berry died in a car crash on the way to Canada
473.s: Chu Berry's car overturned near Youngstown on the way to the Peace Bridge; the bus found him, he died days later and Cab announced it in Montreal; Ike Quebec's predecessor Mac Rae filled in.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: Yeah, not too much of a soloist, you know. Just arranger's piano. Maybe you'll see him in that picture, "Sensations of '44," where they've got one piano over there, another one over there.
